altitude.note: Same ice-surface elevation as the rest of the South Pole station area (reused from the icecube workstream's facility record for consistency, not independently re-measured for ARA).
altitude.quote: IceCube ... located near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station

coordinates.note: No ARA-specific official page publishes station-level latitude/longitude; ARA's own overview paper places it only relative to IceCube ('about 2 km from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory'). Following the precedent set by the icecube workstream's own site:south-pole-icecube record (same physical station, same problem), the geographic South Pole is recorded as an approximate anchor point with a generous precision_m to cover both the IceCube array footprint and ARA's ~2 km offset from it; this is not a surveyed position. src:icecube-official-detector-page is an icecube-workstream source, cited here (not created here) because it independently establishes that IceCube -- and by the 2 km offset, ARA -- sits at the geographic South Pole.
coordinates.quote: IceCube, the South Pole neutrino observatory, is a cubic-kilometer particle detector made of Antarctic ice and located near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station. / [ARA overview paper:] located about 2 km from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory

depth.quote: deployed at a depth of 100-200 m over the period 2012-2018

name: South Pole — ARA stations
notes: facility_id references facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station, owned by the icecube workstream; not created here, per the ID registry and this workstream's brief (ARA is explicitly scoped as 'a new site under the existing facility').

summary.plain: A handful of boreholes near the South Pole, about two kilometres from the IceCube observatory, each holding a small station of radio antennas listening for neutrinos.
summary.technical: ARA station field at the geographic South Pole, ~2 km from the IceCube in-ice array, with stations deployed 100-200 m deep in the ice sheet.
